clue.text: A native American philosopher of old

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a member of an Iroquois people of New York State
second meaning: the Roman Stoic thinker and tutor of Nero

explanation.surface: Some ancient sage who was supposedly an indigenous American.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one person, but it splits after American: two separate meanings of one name.
explanation.definitionFit: Seneca names both a tribe of the Iroquois confederacy and the first-century Roman Stoic writer.

clue.text: Concern one's caught by in lonely place

indicators.note: in places the preceding pair of letters inside the word for a lonely place

parts.note: solitude is a lonely place or state
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone worried about being trapped in an isolated spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's caught by' is read as one with caught set beside it, and that pair sits inside the lonely place.
explanation.definitionFit: Solicitude is anxious care or worry for someone, so it is a formal synonym of concern.

clue.text: Wanderer just not made to stop early

indicators.note: stopping early means the word loses its final letter before it is used

parts.note: no is a word of refusal, a plain not
taken as written before it is cut short

explanation.surface: A traveller who simply was not built to give up early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' is only a joining word here, meaning simply.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad is a member of a people with no fixed home, who wanders from place to place.

clue.text: Group playing music of Prince Albert?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small ensemble, especially of early instruments
second meaning: Victoria's husband held the title of Prince ...

explanation.surface: Asking which band played the tunes Queen Victoria's husband liked.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags Albert as an example: he was the husband of a reigning queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A consort is both an early-music ensemble and the spouse of a reigning monarch, as Albert was.

clue.text: Opening words of page don't get to point — there is one in there

parts.note: p is the standard abbreviation for page

indicators.note: in there says the single item is set inside the phrase just mentioned

parts.note: to ramble is to talk on without reaching the point
one point of the compass: east

explanation.surface: A complaint that the introduction to a page waffles on without getting to the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' means one point of the compass, east, which sits after the first letter of the waffling word.
explanation.definitionFit: A preamble is an introductory statement, the words that open a document or speech.

clue.text: Ballroom dance showing a degree of spirit?

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane
a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A dance that reveals a measure of team spirit or alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A degree of spirit' looks like a measure of strength, but it is a degree (BA) placed after the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban dance taken up in ballroom competition as one of the Latin dances.

clue.text: Shrub that's Arabian though seen all over America

parts.note: Ar. is a dictionary abbreviation for Arabian or Arabic
but and though both introduce a contrast
the United States

explanation.surface: A bush said to be from Arabia yet found growing across the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen all over' only places America at the end; the three abbreviations simply run on.
explanation.definitionFit: Arbutus is the genus of evergreen shrubs and small trees that includes the strawberry tree.

clue.text: Friend chasing book on English porcelain

indicators.note: chasing means coming behind, so this piece goes after the others

parts.note: b is the abbreviation for book
taken as written
the abbreviation for English
Cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate

explanation.surface: A pal pursuing a book about English pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: China for friend is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate), common in British crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone china is a fine porcelain made with bone ash, a speciality of English potteries.

clue.text: Queen opens very large London landmark

indicators.note: opening something means standing at its front, so the monarch comes first

parts.note: Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: The Queen formally opens an enormous new attraction in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opens' suggests a ribbon-cutting, but it only puts the Queen at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The statue popularly called Eros stands over the fountain in Piccadilly Circus, a famous sight of the capital.

clue.text: His paper beat stone

indicators.note: beat in the sense of battered: the words are knocked out of shape

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Rock-paper-scissors gone wrong: his paper beat the stone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface borrows the hand game where paper beats stone; beat is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapphire is a precious gemstone, and stone is the usual crossword word for a gem.

clue.text: Lamb cooked with melon and herb

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are mixed into something new

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe: lamb prepared with melon and a sprig of something green.
explanation.walkthrough: The herb reads like the last ingredient of the dish, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon balm is an aromatic plant of the mint family whose leaves are used as a culinary herb.

clue.text: Throw away turn in game

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it in the rubbish
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: A player discards on their turn during a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo is a game of chance in which numbers drawn at random are marked off on cards.

clue.text: Rules for working QSBDUJDF as a cipher with letters moved one on?

parts.words: QSBDUJDF as a cipher with letters moved one on?
parts.note: surface reading: a puzzle about breaking a simple letter-shift cipher

parts.words: QSBDUJDF as a cipher with letters moved one on?
parts.note: setter's reading: move each letter back one place and the jumble becomes an everyday word for habitual doing, and this jumble is the coded form of it

explanation.surface: A spy's handbook explaining a shift cipher applied to a nonsense string.
explanation.walkthrough: Shift each letter of QSBDUJDF back one (Q to P, S to R and so on) to get PRACTICE; the jumble is literally the code of PRACTICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A code of practice is a set of written guidelines on how a profession or trade should conduct its work.

clue.text: Ship's heaviest load shifting added endless delay, we hear

indicators.note: shifting letters moves them around into another order
without an end, so the word drops its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before it is shortened and rearranged

indicators.note: we hear points to a word picked up by the ear rather than the eye

parts.note: a wait is a delay; it sounds like a measure of heaviness

explanation.surface: Cargo moving around on board caused a long hold-up.
explanation.walkthrough: ADDED without its last D is ADDE, rearranged as DEAD; WAIT spoken gives WEIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's deadweight is the total weight of cargo, fuel and stores it can carry, its maximum load.

clue.text: Understood tax cut made by Channel Islands finally caught on

indicators.note: a cut word has been trimmed, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before it is trimmed
the standard abbreviation for the Channel Islands

indicators.note: finally picks out only the very end of the next word

parts.note: the last letter of caught

explanation.surface: A tax reduction granted to the Channel Islands has become popular.
explanation.walkthrough: TAX loses its X to give TA, then CI and T: TACIT. The Channel Islands lie off Normandy and are a low-tax jurisdiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means implied or understood without being stated openly, as in a tacit agreement.

clue.text: Bird, gigantic one climbing a moment before storm

indicators.note: before places the moment ahead of the storm word in the line
in a down clue climbing means read upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: the roc is the giant bird of Arabian legend
mo is short for moment, as in half a mo
to rant is to storm on angrily

explanation.surface: A huge bird soaring just before a storm breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gigantic one' looks like a giant, but it is a giant bird: the roc. Upwards it reads COR, then MO and RANT.
explanation.definitionFit: The cormorant is a large dark fish-eating seabird with a hooked bill.

clue.text: A lack of fairness in only having cold water?

parts.note: taken as written
just and only both mean merely
ice is frozen, very cold water

explanation.surface: Complaining that it is unfair to be given nothing but cold water.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'in just ice', which is a playful description of having only cold water.
explanation.definitionFit: Injustice is the absence of justice, an unfair act or state, which is a lack of fairness.

clue.text: Shrub with doubled heads exhibited by James Powell and Nigel Carr

indicators.note: a head twice over means taking the opening pair of letters of each name

parts.note: the opening two letters of James
the opening two letters of Powell
the opening two letters of Nigel
the opening two letters of Carr

explanation.surface: A plant with double flower heads shown by two gardeners at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubled heads' sounds like a horticultural feature, but it asks for two leading letters from each of the four names.
explanation.definitionFit: Japonica is the common name for the flowering quince, an ornamental shrub from Japan.

clue.text: Not requiring much filthy lucre?

parts.note: surface reading: something that does not cost much money
setter's reading: filthy lucre is money, and filth is soil, so the low price is put in terms of muck

explanation.walkthrough: Filthy lucre is a jocular phrase for money; the answer echoes its filth by pairing a word for muck with a word for inexpensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirt cheap means extremely inexpensive, costing very little money.

clue.text: Cutter or some other boat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tool for trimming, such as hair or nail shears
second meaning: a fast nineteenth-century sailing ship

explanation.walkthrough: A cutter is also a kind of boat, so the clue seems to ask for an alternative vessel; the first word is the tool sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a trimming implement and a fast square-rigged merchant ship such as the Cutty Sark.

clue.text: Burn last of diseased vegetable crop

parts.note: to char is to scorch or burn

indicators.note: last of picks out only the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the final letter of diseased

explanation.surface: Farmers burning a blighted field of vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Chard is a leafy beet grown as a vegetable crop for its stalks and leaves.

clue.text: Shorten hanging material, making new length

indicators.note: making here means turning one letter into another inside the word

parts.note: a curtain is fabric hung at a window
n is the abbreviation for new
l is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: Taking up the drapes by cutting new fabric to length.
explanation.walkthrough: In CURTAIN the final N (new) is changed into L (length).
explanation.definitionFit: To curtail is to cut short or reduce, so it is a synonym of shorten.

clue.text: Steal from distraught connoisseur this classic book

parts.note: to rob is to steal from

indicators.note: distraught means deeply upset, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A thief takes a rare first edition from a heartbroken collector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This classic book' sounds like the stolen item, but it defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's 1719 novel about a castaway is one of the classics of English literature.

clue.text: Cook's greeting to officer out of line

indicators.note: out of means the letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: soldiers salute an officer as a greeting
l is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A ship's or army cook greets an officer improperly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook's' is cook is: the definition plus a link. SALUTE loses its L to give SAUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To sauté is to cook food quickly in a little fat, so it is one specific way of cooking.

clue.text: Act as informer about introduction of long-range ballistic weapon

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police

indicators.note: an introduction is the start, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter of long-range

explanation.surface: A spy reporting on the launch of a new long-range missile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long-range ballistic weapon' reads as a missile, but only one letter of long-range is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A sling is a strap for hurling stones, a weapon that throws projectiles, hence ballistic.

clue.text: Repetition more than once in speech of Pumblechook

indicators.note: in says the letters are found inside the name that follows

parts.note: found inside the name, after the first six letters

explanation.surface: A comment on the repetitive way a Dickens character talks.
explanation.walkthrough: Pumblechook is Pip's pompous uncle in Great Expectations, given to saying things over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound reflected back and heard again, often several times, so it is repeated sound.

clue.text: Millions enter to applaud band getting things together

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: to clap is to applaud
m is the abbreviation for millions

explanation.surface: Huge crowds arrive to cheer a pop group that is reforming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a music group, but it means a strap; M goes into CLAP: CLA(M)P.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamp is a brace or band that holds two things firmly together.

clue.text: Continuous relaxation after new clubs opened by university

indicators.note: opened by puts the college piece at the very front of the pair
after places the rest word behind the opening letters

parts.note: u is the abbreviation for university
n is the abbreviation for new
c is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
easing is a slackening or relaxation

explanation.surface: A university keeps opening new clubs, with ongoing relaxation of rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Unceasing means never stopping, which is a synonym of continuous.

clue.text: Up to the planned level — unfortunately not great

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone awry, so the letters come out in a different order

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A disappointed report that results reached the target but were nothing special.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface contradicts itself: the answer means meeting the goal, while 'not great' is just its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: On target means meeting the planned standard or goal, as a project on target for completion.

clue.text: Escape using key with window

parts.note: F is a musical key
a light is a window, especially a pane in a larger window

explanation.surface: A prisoner breaks out with a key and through a window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like a door key, but it is a musical key, a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Flight is the act of running away, as in taking flight, a synonym of escape.
